data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
learningPoints: Strengthens control of reported speech and tense backshifting.
Builds accuracy with said vs told distinctions.
Improves comprehension of reported information in listening tasks.
Develops structured communication for formal writing.
Prepares you for academic and workplace reporting contexts.
ESOL B2 and aligns with IELTS 6.0–6.5 and TOEFL iBT 72–94 score ranges.

sections.summary: Backshift present simple to past simple in reported speech.
sections.explain: In reported speech, present simple usually changes to past simple.

words.word: She said she worked in a hospital.
She said she works in a hospital.
She said she is work in a hospital.

sections.explain: In reported speech, 'will' usually changes to 'would'.

words.word: He said he would apply for the job.
He said he will apply for the job.
He said he would applied for the job.

sections.explain: 'Told' requires a person: told me, told her, etc.

words.word: She told me she was tired.
She told that she was tired.
She said me she was tired.

sections.explain: 'Said' does not take a direct object without a preposition.

words.word: He said that the meeting was cancelled.
He said me that the meeting was cancelled.
He told that the meeting was cancelled.

sections.explain: Past continuous usually remains past continuous in reporting.

words.word: She said she was studying when I called.
She said she is studying when I called.
She said she studies when I called.

sections.summary: Backshift present perfect to past perfect.
sections.explain: Present perfect often changes to past perfect in reported speech.

words.word: He said he had finished the report.
He said he has finished the report.
He said he finished the report already.

sections.explain: Reported yes/no questions use 'if' or 'whether' and statement word order.

words.word: She asked if I was available.
She asked was I available.
She asked if was I available.

sections.summary: Report wh-questions using statement word order.
sections.explain: Reported wh-questions use statement word order, not question order.

words.word: He asked where I lived.
He asked where did I live.
He asked where I live.
She said she could help us.
She said she can help us.
She said she will can help us.

sections.summary: Time expression shift in reported speech.
sections.explain: Time expressions often change (e.g., today → that day).

words.word: He said he would start the project the next day.
He said he will start the project tomorrow.
He said he would start the project tomorrow.
